candidates.title: Are We Ready For An Agent-Native Memory System?
candidates.summary: Systematic experimental study treating agent memory as a data management system, decomposing it into representation/storage, extraction, retrieval/routing, and maintenance modules, and benchmarking 12 memory systems across 11 datasets to expose operational cost and architectural tradeoffs.

candidates.title: TokenPilot: Cache-Efficient Context Management for LLM Agents
candidates.summary: Dual-granularity context management framework (Ingestion-Aware Compaction + Lifecycle-Aware Eviction) that preserves prompt-cache continuity for long agent sessions, reducing inference cost 56-87% on PinchBench and Claw-Eval; integrated into LightMem2 with open-source code.

candidates.title: Governed Shared Memory for Multi-Agent LLM Systems
candidates.summary: Formalizes the 'fleet-memory problem' for cooperating LLM agents and proposes systems primitives (scoped retrieval, temporal supersession, provenance tracking, policy-governed propagation) implemented in the MemClaw reference system, evaluated via the ArgusFleet harness.

deep_entry_contract.boundary: Cross-region/WAN/cross-cluster transfer, migration, remote access, bandwidth reduction, or consistency must be a core evaluated problem; local KV compression or tokenization alone does not qualify.
